rules.title: Close every section header bracket
rules.message: Section header has unbalanced brackets.
rules.explanation: Genius guidance establishes bracketed section headers. Detecting a missing delimiter is also a product-safety rule from the parser contract, not an explicit Genius catalog of every malformed case.

rules.title: Only italic and bold performer markup
rules.message: Unsupported performer markup.
rules.explanation: Performer differentiation supports plain, italic, bold, and nested bold-italic slots. This literal tag or malformed nesting is preserved for review.

rules.title: The selected language matches the lyrics
rules.message: Lyrics appear to be French, but English is selected.
rules.explanation: Language recognition runs locally using statistical text analysis. Review the selected lyric language; short, mixed-language, and transliterated songs may be inconclusive.
rules.flaggedExample:
[Verse]
Je regarde la lumière du matin
Et je sais que tu resteras avec moi ce soir
rules.acceptedExample:
[Verse]
I see the morning light through every shadow
And I know that you will stay with me tonight

rules.title: Every song part has a header
rules.message: This lyric section has no header.
rules.explanation: Every blank-line lyric section needs a song-part header. If these lines continue the previous song part, remove the blank line instead—Genius does not allow blank lines to split one part into smaller stanzas. Otherwise, choose a reviewed localized term or enter a custom header; the source text remains unchanged until confirmation.

rules.title: Name every section header
rules.message: This section header is empty.
rules.explanation: The brackets are here, but the song part they open is not named, so this line marks nothing. Choose a reviewed header for the language you are transcribing in — LyricLint writes the name between the brackets you already typed and leaves the rest of the line, a performer legend included, exactly as it is.

rules.title: Song part names go in brackets
rules.message: Write this section header as [Verse 1].
rules.explanation: Genius marks song parts with a bracketed header. “Verse 1:” names a reviewed song part but is written as a plain line, so it reads as a lyric and no section is created. The bracketed form keeps the same part name.

rules.title: A blank line before a header
rules.message: Add a blank line before this section header.
rules.explanation: The reviewed Genius guidance places headers above distinct song parts but does not explicitly require a blank line. LyricLint suggests one here to make section changes easier to scan.

rules.title: Headers from the selected language
rules.message: “Verse” conflicts with the reviewed Norwegian header pack.
rules.explanation: This is a recognized English Verse header. The selected reviewed language pack recommends a localized term; custom and unreviewed headers are always preserved.

rules.title: Prefer the localized song part name
rules.message: Use the reviewed Norwegian header “Bro” instead of “Bridge”.
rules.explanation: The Genius international section-header source recognizes “Bro” as the Norwegian term for “Bridge”. Using the reviewed header keeps the transcription aligned with the selected language pack.

rules.title: Check an unrecognized header
rules.message: Review the custom section header “Chor”.
rules.explanation: “Chor” is not in any reviewed section-header catalog. It may be intentional, but it could also be a typo. Confirm it manually; LyricLint preserves the text and does not guess a replacement.

rules.title: [Hook] is deprecated
rules.message: The [Hook] section name is deprecated.
rules.explanation: The current Genius section guide replaces [Hook] with [Chorus] or [Refrain]. Choose the term that matches the song structure.

rules.title: One header for an immediate repeat
rules.message: Keep an immediately repeated song part under one header.
rules.explanation: This section exactly repeats the song part immediately before it. Genius keeps the repeated lyrics, but places both copies together under the same header without a blank separator.

rules.title: Link repeated song parts
rules.message: Link these repeats so one correction reaches them all.
rules.explanation: This song part appears 2 times, and every copy either already matches the others or is still empty. Linking ties them together so that editing one edits the rest, and a correction can never land in only one copy. Nothing is overwritten: the words the copies already disagree on are kept exactly as they are and left out of the link, so a chorus that changes one line at the end can still be tied to the others.
rules.flaggedExample:
[Chorus]
Hold the line

[Verse 1]
A lyric

[Chorus]
Hold the line

rules.title: Number distinct verses
rules.message: Number this song's verses.
rules.explanation: This song has 2 verses, and each one has different words. The Genius section guide enumerates distinct verses in ascending order, so a reader can tell which verse is which.

rules.title: Styled vocals need a performer legend
rules.message: Styled vocals need a performer legend.
rules.explanation: This multi-performer section differentiates inline vocals but its header does not identify the style slots. Add a performer legend, or remove the formatting if the section no longer needs performer differentiation.

rules.title: Legend styles in slot order
rules.message: Performer legend styles are out of slot order.
rules.explanation: Section-local performer groups should appear in plain, italic, bold, then bold-italic order. Shifting them into order rewrites the legend and the section's formatting as one edit, so every group keeps its own performers.

rules.title: Every inline style is in the legend
rules.message: Inline style has no performer in the section legend.
rules.explanation: The styled lyric is preserved as an unresolved voice. Choose the section voice and this styled voice to add the missing performer legend without changing the lyrics.

rules.title: Style the whole parenthetical
rules.message: Include the parentheses in this performer formatting.
rules.explanation: Everything inside this parenthetical belongs to one styled performer. Leaving either delimiter outside the wrapper assigns that punctuation to the section’s plain performer.

rules.title: Merge adjacent performer markup
rules.message: Adjacent performer formatting can be merged.
rules.explanation: The same performer style ends and immediately starts again on the next line. Keep one wrapper around the continuous passage to minimize formatting markers.

rules.title: No unused legend slots
rules.message: This performer slot is not used in the section.
rules.explanation: The section legend should describe the performer styles that actually occur in its lyrics. Remove the unused slot to keep the header and formatting in sync.

rules.title: More voices than formatting slots
rules.message: This section has more voice groups than the four formatting slots.
rules.explanation: The source discusses omitting names when too many vocalists prevent concise formatting and gives a more-than-four example for multiple vocal samples; it does not state a universal five-performer ban. Preserve the import while considering a merged group, another section, or explicitly removing differentiation.

rules.title: No performer labels on lyric lines
rules.message: Do not label individual lyric lines with bracketed performer names.
rules.explanation: Performer identities belong in the section-header legend and are correlated through the four style slots. Removing the label drops the attribution from the lyric, so name the performer in the section header and style the line to keep it.

rules.title: Standardized lyric spellings
rules.message: Use “I'ma” instead of “Imma”.
rules.explanation: The reviewed Genius spelling guide recommends this form.

rules.title: Match the selected English variant
rules.message: Review this American spelling against the selected British English variant.
rules.explanation: British English accepts “till,” while American English uses “’til.” This is a consistency review, not an automatic replacement.

rules.title: Write texting shorthand out in full
rules.message: Use “I don't know” instead of “Idk”.
rules.explanation: Texting shorthand is a way of writing rather than a way of singing: the letters stand in for words the vocal performs in full, and Genius wants the sung words in standardized spelling. Initialisms that are themselves said aloud — ASAP, OK, VIP — are left alone. Check the delivery before replacing this, since an artist who spells the letters out is transcribed as they sing them.
rules.acceptedExample:
[Verse]
I don't know what to tell you

rules.title: Straight quotes in lyric text
rules.message: Use a straight " instead of the opening curly double quote.
rules.explanation: The exact curly quote can be replaced mechanically. Lines containing unsupported markup are excluded so the fixer never rewrites uncertain markup.

rules.title: Apostrophes in contractions
rules.message: “Dont” looks like a contraction missing an apostrophe.
rules.explanation: This list excludes especially ambiguous forms such as “ill” and “well.” Confirm the intended meaning before applying the punctuation.

rules.title: Capitalize the pronoun “I”
rules.message: The English first-person pronoun “I” should be capitalized.
rules.explanation: Capitalize the standalone pronoun and its initial letter in contractions such as “I’m,” “I’ve,” “I’d,” and “I’ll.”

rules.title: Common English misspellings
rules.message: “definately” is a common English spelling error.
rules.explanation: The standard spelling is “definitely.”

rules.title: Common Norwegian misspellings
rules.message: “desverre” is a common Norwegian spelling error.
rules.explanation: The standard spelling is “dessverre.”

rules.title: Common German misspellings
rules.message: “garnicht” is a common German spelling error.
rules.explanation: The standard spelling is “gar nicht.”

rules.title: Spanish “al” and “del” contractions
rules.message: Contract “a el” to “al” in Spanish.
rules.explanation: Spanish contracts the lowercase prepositions “a” and “de” with the article “el.” Capitalized “El” is left alone because it can belong to a proper name.

rules.title: Common Spanish misspellings
rules.message: “Porfavor” is a common Spanish word-division error.
rules.explanation: The standard spelling is “Por favor.”

rules.title: Common French misspellings
rules.message: “sa va” is a common French spelling error.
rules.explanation: The reviewed standard spelling is “ça va.” The suggestion remains optional because lyrics can preserve intentional forms.

rules.title: Standard Arabic spellings
rules.message: Review “لاكن” as the standard Arabic form “لكن”.
rules.explanation: This is a common standard-Arabic spelling correction, but dialect spelling and intentional lyric stylization can preserve the original form.

rules.title: Standard Japanese spellings
rules.message: Review “こんにちわ” as the standard Japanese spelling “こんにちは”.
rules.explanation: This is the conventional spelling, but phonetic spelling and intentional lyric stylization can preserve the original form.

rules.title: Standard Korean spellings
rules.message: Review “됬” as the standard Korean form “됐”.
rules.explanation: This common spelling correction is offered as a preview so the transcription can retain intentional lyric styling.

rules.title: Spell out symbols in lyrics
rules.message: Spell out this ampersand unless it belongs to a brand name.
rules.explanation: Genius writes this symbol as “and” in lyric text, while preserving it inside brand names. The surrounding spaces make this look like a word rather than a compact brand, but the replacement still needs review.

rules.title: No invisible or trailing whitespace
rules.message: This line ends with invisible whitespace.
rules.explanation: Trailing spaces survive a copy into Genius without ever being visible in the editor. Removing them changes nothing a reader can see, and the parser already treats a whitespace-only line as a blank one, so no section boundary moves.

rules.title: One space between words
rules.message: Use one space between these words.
rules.explanation: Consecutive ordinary spaces between words are mechanically detectable formatting residue. Genius does not state an exact one-space rule, so LyricLint treats this as a text-hygiene suggestion.

rules.title: [?] for an unclear lyric
rules.message: Use [?] for an incomprehensible lyric.
rules.explanation: This is an exact recognized unknown marker, so replacing only the marker is mechanically safe.

rules.title: Question marks are not the [?] marker
rules.message: Genius marks an unclear lyric with [?], not «???».
rules.explanation: A bare run of question marks is the transcriber's own placeholder rather than a marker anyone recognizes, and the same characters can be deliberate punctuation — so the replacement is offered for review instead of applied mechanically.

rules.title: Resolve [?] where you can
rules.message: Try to identify the lyric marked [?].
rules.explanation: Aim to transcribe all audible lyrics. Use [?] only when careful listening still cannot determine what is being sung.

rules.title: Write repeats out in full
rules.message: Write repeated lyrics instead of a section-count placeholder.
rules.explanation: Repeated sections should contain the transcribed lyrics. The placeholder is preserved because expanding it requires the editor to choose the correct source section.

rules.title: Asterisks around a sound effect
rules.message: Use asterisks around this likely sound effect.
rules.explanation: The braces wrap a recognized sound-effect phrase. Confirm the contextual classification before replacing the wrapper.

rules.title: Four asterisks for a censored word
rules.message: A censored word should use exactly four asterisks.
rules.explanation: This mixes letters with an asterisk mask. Confirm before replacing the entire censored-word candidate so no partial spelling remains.

rules.title: Capitalize a parenthesized ad-lib
rules.message: Capitalize this parenthesized ad-lib.
rules.explanation: This is a short recognized ad-lib inside parentheses. The suggestion is contextual and requires preview.

rules.title: Separate consecutive ad-libs
rules.message: Separate these ad-libs with commas, or join them with hyphens.
rules.explanation: One ad-lib follows another with nothing between them. A comma separates them as distinct calls and a hyphen combines them into one; which one fits is a phrasing call, so both edits are preview-only.

rules.title: Capitalize the start of a line
rules.message: This lyric line starts with a lowercase letter.
rules.explanation: Conventional capitalization suggests an uppercase line start, but stylization and continuation can be valid; review the preview in context.

rules.title: Sentence case, not title case
rules.message: This line may be capitalized like a title.
rules.explanation: Lyrics use conventional sentence capitalization rather than capitalizing every word. Review this manually because names, acronyms, and intentional styling can look similar.
rules.flaggedExample:
[Verse]
This Is The Way We Live
Every Single Word Starts Uppercase
rules.acceptedExample:
[Verse]
This is the way we live
Every single word starts normally

rules.title: No period at the end of a line
rules.message: Lyric lines should not end with a period.
rules.explanation: Apple Music lyric guidance explicitly excludes commas and periods at line endings. The current Genius guide separately requires question marks for questions and uses exclamation marks for excitement, but does not state the same blanket ban. Removal is preview-only so quotations, abbreviations, and intentional delivery remain reviewable.

rules.title: A question mark on a question
rules.message: This clearly interrogative line may need a question mark.
rules.explanation: The line begins with a strong question construction. Punctuation can still depend on delivery, so insertion is preview-only.

rules.title: No comma after an em dash
rules.message: Do not follow an em dash with a comma.
rules.explanation: The comma directly after the em dash is mechanically detectable, but the punctuation change remains preview-only.

rules.title: Break a prose-like line
rules.message: This line reads like several lyric lines combined.
rules.explanation: Multiple clauses and a high word count make the transcription look prose-like. There is no fixed character limit; listen for musical line breaks and split only when supported by phrasing.
rules.flaggedExample:
[Verse]
I walked into the room, and everyone was talking; the lights were fading, while another story started and nobody stopped to breathe before the ending arrived.

rules.title: Spell out small numbers
rules.message: Consider spelling out “5” as “five”.
rules.explanation: This small standalone number is outside the reviewed time, money, percentage, date, and compound-number exceptions. Delivery or naming can still matter, so the edit requires preview.

harper.behavior: Alongside the reviewed Genius rules, LyricLint runs Harper, a local English proofreader, in the browser. Its findings arrive as spelling.harper, grammar.harper, and style.harper — always suggestions, always citing Harper itself (T-HARPER) rather than a Genius guideline, and a native reviewed rule always wins where the two overlap.
limitations: English only; it does not run for the other reviewed languages.
Its suggestions are general proofreading, not reviewed Genius policy, and have no reference pages.
Prose-assuming readability measures are filtered out, because lyrics use deliberate fragments, dialect, repetition, and nonstandard spelling.
It is seeded with the reviewed preferred spellings and the draft’s performer names so it does not fight the Genius-specific rules.

policyNotes:
Policy
LyricLint does not claim that a rule is authoritative merely because it appears on a Genius page.

A production lint rule requires:

- An exact policy-source URL. Any behavior described as a Genius rule requires an exact Genius
  URL or annotation ID.
- A locally stored source title and rule paraphrase.
- A last-verified date.
- Human review of the interpretation.
- Tests covering valid, invalid, and ambiguous examples.

Community annotations can change. Rule data is versioned, reviewed, and bundled with the application. Live scraping is not part of the editing path.

The content-language mismatch check is a product-safety diagnostic rather than
a Genius policy claim. It uses a bundled statistical detector, runs locally,
and links to the detector implementation as tooling provenance.

The line-ending comma/period check is cross-platform guidance, not a direct Genius policy
claim. Apple Music for Artists explicitly disallows both marks at the end of a lyric line.
Genius's current verified guide does not state that blanket ban; its punctuation annotation
instead requires question marks for questions and reserves exclamation marks for excitement.
LyricLint records both sources and keeps removal preview-only.

The blank-line-before-header check is a LyricLint readability suggestion, not a direct Genius
policy claim. The reviewed Genius source establishes that headers sit above distinct song parts
but does not explicitly require an empty line before each header.

The texting-shorthand check is a LyricLint reading of two reviewed Genius sources rather than a
distinct annotation of its own. No verified Genius page names `idk` or `ur`. What the sources do
establish is that lyrics use standardized spellings and reflect what is actually sung, and
written-only shorthand is neither: the letters are a way of writing words the vocal performs in
full. The rule therefore stays a suggestion with preview-only fixes, and it is deliberately silent
on initialisms that are themselves said aloud, where expanding one would assert something about
the delivery that no source supports.

Reviewed guidance without a text-only diagnostic
- Quotation marks depend on whether a phrase names a song, quotes speech, or refers to a word.
- Pronunciation depends on the recording; the linter can only keep affected spelling fixes out of bulk fixing.
- `[Instrumental]` is already a recognized section name, but only song-page metadata can establish that the whole track is instrumental.
- Translation and romanization separation is page-level metadata, not a property of the canonical lyric string.
